summary: Santa Cruz County, CA lookout tower built by the CCC in 1934 and dedicated in 1938; burned to the ground on August 4, 2018. No source describes what remains now.

facts.design: lookout tower on a summit; the sources read give no height or cab details
facts.status_note: Burned to the ground on August 4, 2018; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site now
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry (called the California Division of Forestry in a 1975 story and a local wiki)

staffing.status: staffed by veteran lookout Clifford 'Mac' McLaughlin, who said he had spent 17 years there; he gave up the post in October 1975

visit.trail_note: A guide page describes an unpaved, 4WD summit road starting from Empire Grade; a local wiki describes the Eagle Rock Trail through Little Basin; no current access notice was found in the sources read

events.note: Under erection in November 1934, with CCC men from the Big Basin camp put to work on it; a 2018 report credits the CCC with building it
Dedication of the new tower was previewed in a July 1938 newspaper item for the next day
A 1975 story says Clifford 'Mac' McLaughlin had spent 17 years at the tower and had given up the post
Burned to the ground on August 4, 2018; Cal Fire named the vegetation fire the Eagle Fire

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 newspaper shows erection under way in November 1934; the 2018 report gives 1934 as the build year; the July 1938 item previews a dedication of the new tower. We record 1934 as built and 1938 as the dedication.
The Forest Lookouts header says California Department of Forestry; the 1975 story and the local wiki say California Division of Forestry. Both names appear in the sources; we report both.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 152.4 (500 ft) is not supported by any source read, so it is not in facts; please check before keeping it. The 1934 build and 2018 burn are well supported. No current access or ownership source was found; the road and trail details come from a guide page of unknown date and a local wiki, and the Little Basin ownership point is from a local wiki. The FFLA index row for the Santa Cruz Eagle Rock reads Gone with no registry number, which fits the burn. Brief events are otherwise consistent with the sources.
